title: Zeroth cohomology computes maps to an injective single object
statement: Let A be an abelian category with a chosen derived category whose Hom types are in universe w. For every K in D(A) and injective I in A, the map on morphisms induced by H⁰, from Hom_D(A)(K,I[0]) to Hom_A(H⁰(K),H⁰(I[0])), is bijective. No Grothendieck or coproduct hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proof step 1: comparison Hom_D(K,I[0]) with Hom_A(H⁰(K),I) for injective I

proof.text: Represent K by a complex C. The bounded-below injective complex I[0] is K-injective, so derived maps to it are chain maps modulo homotopy. A chain map is a map C⁰ -> I vanishing on boundaries. For a map H⁰(C) -> I, injectivity extends it from cycles modulo boundaries to C⁰ modulo boundaries; this gives a chain map inducing the prescribed map on H⁰. If the induced map on H⁰ is zero, the component C⁰ -> I factors through C⁰/Z⁰(C), the image of C⁰ -> C¹. Extend this map from the image to C¹ by injectivity to obtain a null homotopy. Transport through the canonical localization and single-object homology isomorphisms. This proves bijectivity of the stated, specific homology map.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_homology_injective_bijective
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (K : DerivedCategory A) (I : A) [Injective I] :
    Function.Bijective
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A 0).map :
        (K ⟶ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj I) →
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A 0).obj K ⟶
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A 0).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj I)))
